entries.title: daemon: release the lock on stop and reclaim a dead-owner lock, so restart recovers in seconds
entries.body:
*agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Summary
Every `agentflow restart` currently leaves the daemon down for up to **3 hours**. A clean stop strands the daemon's lock; the replacement daemon sees a still-fresh lock, logs `another daemon is running; exiting`, and the launch agent retries every ~10s to the same dead end until the stranded lock finally ages past the 3-hour stale threshold. Fix it in the daemon so a stop leaves no lock behind, and a crash's stranded lock is reclaimed on the next launch — not after 3 hours.

## Verified
Against `agentflow/daemon.py` in this checkout:
- **Lock strands on stop.** `main()` calls `_release_lock()` only from its `finally` block. There is no SIGTERM/SIGINT handler anywhere in the module (confirmed: no `signal` import, no `SIGTERM`). `agentflow stop`/`restart` → `launchctl bootout` → SIGTERM → Python's default handler terminates the process without running `finally`, so the lock directory (holding its `pid` file, mtime frozen) is left behind on **every** clean stop.
- **Recovery waits 3 hours.** `_acquire_lock()` only reclaims a lock once its age exceeds `STALE_SECONDS = 3 * 3600`. A restart's `stop`→`start` gap is ~1s, so the new daemon sees a <3h lock and refuses (`another daemon is running; exiting`).
- **The owner is already knowable.** `_try_claim()` writes the owner pid to `LOCK/pid`, and `_owns_lock()` reads it back — so the daemon can already distinguish a dead owner from a live one, but the acquire path never uses that; it only checks mtime age.
- **The wrapper's `rmdir` self-heal is not in this repo.** The `scripts/agentflow` wrapper the issue cites lives in the separate **dotfiles** repo (`rmdir "$LOCK"` on a non-empty dir → silently fails). That half is out of scope here (see Out of scope). Moving crash-recovery into the daemon makes the wrapper's `rm -rf` redundant rather than load-bearing.

## Current behavior
- Clean stop/restart: lock stranded 100% of the time.
- Time to recover after a restart: up to **3 hours** (until `STALE_SECONDS` elapses), during which the launch agent loops `clearing stale lock` / `another daemon is running; exiting` every ~10s.
- A true crash (`kill -9`): same 3-hour wait, since the daemon has no fast crash-recovery of its own.

## Desired behavior
- A clean stop (`stop`/`restart`/`bootout`) releases the lock as it exits, so **no** lock is stranded and the next daemon starts immediately.
- If a lock *is* found on startup and its recorded owner pid is **not a live process**, the new daemon reclaims it right away rather than waiting for the 3-hour age-out — so even a `kill -9` crash self-heals on the next launch, entirely within the daemon.
- A restart reliably brings the daemon back **within seconds**, with no `another daemon is running` loop.

## Key interfaces
Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.
- `agentflow/daemon.py`: `main()` (install the SIGTERM/SIGINT handling around the existing `try/finally`), `_acquire_lock()` / `_try_claim()` (add the dead-owner reclaim, reusing the `LOCK/pid` the code already writes), `_release_lock()`/`_owns_lock()` (the release path — already pid-guarded so it never removes another daemon's lock).
- **Traps:**
  - The heartbeat runs in a `daemon=True` background thread; the signal must be handled on the **main** thread and drive the existing `finally` (e.g. raise so `finally` runs once) — don't add a second, racing release path, and keep release idempotent so a signal mid-shutdown doesn't double-unlink.
  - Preserve the existing **race safety**: the stale reclaim uses an atomic `os.rename` so exactly one of many racing starters wins. A dead-owner reclaim must keep that exactly-one guarantee (see `test_stale_lock_reclaim_is_exclusive`) and must never reclaim a lock whose pid is *alive* (pid could be the current healthy daemon; guard against pid-reuse false positives — the mtime/heartbeat path still backstops).
  - Don't remove a lock owned by a live *other* daemon — `test_release_leaves_another_pids_lock_alone` must still pass.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] After a SIGTERM to the running daemon (what `bootout`/`stop` sends), the lock directory is gone — nothing stranded.
- [ ] `agentflow restart` brings the daemon back within seconds; the log shows no repeated `another daemon is running; exiting`.
- [ ] On startup, a lock whose recorded pid is a dead process is reclaimed immediately — **without** waiting for `STALE_SECONDS` (3h) — so a `kill -9`'d daemon self-heals on next launch.
- [ ] A lock whose recorded pid is a **live** process is still refused (no takeover of a healthy daemon); the existing exclusive-reclaim and heartbeat tests still pass.
- [ ] **Regression test** in `tests/test_daemon.py`: simulate the stop→start path — a daemon that receives SIGTERM releases its lock, and a fresh `_acquire_lock()` then succeeds — and a separate test that a lock stamped with a dead pid is reclaimed at once while a lock stamped with a live pid is not. These would fail against today's `finally`-only release and age-only reclaim.

## Out of scope
- The **dotfiles** wrapper (`scripts/agentflow`): the `rmdir`→`rm -rf` self-heal and the `restart` `sleep 1`→wait-for-exit change. Those live in a different repo; once the daemon self-heals a dead-owner lock, the wrapper's clear is belt-and-suspenders, not required — track it separately if wanted.
- Do **not** lower `STALE_SECONDS` or touch the heartbeat interval — the dead-owner check is the fast path; the age-out stays as the backstop.
- No new CLI verbs, no changes to `start`/`stop`/`status` output beyond what falls out of the fix.

<!-- agentflow:original-below -->
<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

## Symptom

Every `agentflow restart` leaves the daemon dead. The log fills with pairs like:

```
agentflow[wrapper]: clearing stale lock
agentflow: another daemon is running; exiting
```

repeating every ~10s (the KeepAlive throttle). The daemon does not come back on its own until the stranded lock ages past the 3h stale threshold — so a "restart" silently means "down for up to 3 hours" unless someone clears the lock by hand.

## Root cause — two compounding bugs

**1. The wrapper's self-heal can't actually clear the lock.**
`scripts/agentflow` (`__daemon`) tries to clear a crash-stranded lock with `rmdir "$LOCK"`. But the lock is a *directory containing a `pid` file* (`daemon.py` `_try_claim` writes `LOCK/pid`). `rmdir` only removes empty directories, so it fails — and the failure is swallowed by `2>/dev/null || true`. The "clearing stale lock" line prints, but nothing is cleared.

**2. The lock leaks on every `stop`.**
`_release_lock()` runs only in `main()`'s `finally`. `agentflow stop` → `launchctl bootout` → SIGTERM, and Python's default SIGTERM handler terminates the process without running `finally`. So the lock dir (with its `pid` file, mtime frozen) is stranded on every clean stop/restart.

Together: `restart` = `stop` (strands lock) → 1s → `start`. The new daemon sees a <3h-old lock, exits "another daemon is running". KeepAlive retries every 10s with the same result until the lock finally ages out (`STALE_SECONDS = 3*3600`).

## Immediate remediation (already applied by hand)
`launchctl bootout …` → `rm -rf ~/.agentflow/daemon.lock` → `launchctl bootstrap …`. Daemon is back up.

## Proposed fix (to be grilled)

Fix **both** halves — either alone is insufficient:

- **Release the lock on SIGTERM/SIGINT.** Install a signal handler in the daemon that runs `_release_lock()` (or raises so the `finally` fires) so a normal `stop`/`bootout` leaves no lock behind. This is the real fix — a clean stop should never strand a lock.
- **Make the wrapper's self-heal correct** as belt-and-suspenders: replace `rmdir "$LOCK"` with something that removes a non-empty dir (`rm -rf`), and only when `daemon_pid` is empty (as it already gates). This still matters for the genuine crash case (SIGKILL, panic) where no handler can run.
- Consider whether `restart`'s `sleep 1` should instead *wait for the process to actually exit* before `start`, to close the overlap window.

## Acceptance
- `agentflow restart` reliably brings the daemon back within seconds, no "another daemon is running" loop.
- A `kill -9` of the daemon (true crash) still self-heals on next launch via the wrapper (lock actually removed).
- A test exercises the stop→start path and asserts the lock does not strand a live daemon out.

</details>

entries.title: Mockup phase: notify maintainer when variants are ready
entries.body:
> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Agent Brief

**Summary**

Notify the maintainer when the mockup phase posts a variant round ready for selection, and send a distinct notification when the phase posts `MISSING-CONTEXT:` instead.

**Verified**

No read-only real-data pull is declared for this repository, so verification is code-path based. `intake_once` makes 1 `agentflow needs you` notification when an issue is initially routed to `needs-mockup`. `produce_once` makes 0 notification calls across all of its current outcomes. Its success branch reports `drew mockup variants` solely from the session's successful exit, without confirming what comment was posted.

The premise holds: `PRODUCE_PROMPT` permits a session that cannot draw variants to post 1 `MISSING-CONTEXT:` comment using the same mockup disclaimer. `_has_mockup_variants` recognizes that disclaimer's `MOCKUP_MARK`, so `_mockup_eligible` will not select the issue again. Today that stuck outcome also produces 0 notifications.

**Current behavior**

A mockup issue generates 1 notification at park time and 0 when its variants become actionable. A session that errors or times out without posting generates 0 notifications and can retry after its drawing claim is released. A posted `MISSING-CONTEXT:` result also generates 0 notifications, but the shared marker prevents another variant round from being selected.

**Desired behavior**

After `produce_once` confirms that the session posted a genuine variant round, make exactly 1 best-effort `agentflow needs you` notification whose click target is the issue. If the posted result is `MISSING-CONTEXT:`, make exactly 1 distinct needs-you notification explaining that the mockup is stuck. A successful process exit without either confirmed comment is not a successful variant round and must not ping. Errors, timeouts, provisioning failures, capacity deferrals, and other outcomes with no posted result must remain silent and preserve their existing retry behavior.

Keep the existing single park-time notification unchanged. The new notification occurs later, when the produced result becomes actionable; it must not add another notification to the intake/park branch.

**Key interfaces**

Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers:

- `produce_once` — owns the drawing session lifecycle and should trigger notifications only after classifying the result actually posted on the issue.
- `PRODUCE_PROMPT`, `_MOCKUP_DISCLAIMER`, and `MOCKUP_MARK` — distinguish a genuine variant round from the allowed `MISSING-CONTEXT:` result; do not treat a successful `launch` boolean alone as proof that variants were posted.
- `_has_mockup_variants` and `_mockup_eligible` — existing one-round dedup and retry behavior are traps to preserve unless the separate marker-conflation work explicitly changes them.
- `notify` — reuse the existing best-effort needs-you transport and point its click URL at the issue.
- `intake_once` — already sends the 1 park-time notification; do not add another call on that branch.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] One confirmed genuine variant-round comment causes exactly 1 `agentflow needs you` notification attempt, with the issue as its click target.
- [ ] The success notification is emitted only after the variant-round post is confirmed, not merely because the drawing process exited successfully.
- [ ] One posted `MISSING-CONTEXT:` result causes exactly 1 distinct needs-you notification and does not also send the variant-ready notification.
- [ ] A session that errors or times out without posting causes 0 notifications and remains eligible for the existing next-cycle retry.
- [ ] No issue, no available pool, or worktree/provision failure causes 0 notifications.
- [ ] Initial routing to `needs-mockup` still causes exactly 1 park-time notification; the new behavior does not duplicate that branch's ping.
- [ ] Regression tests exercise these outcomes through `produce_once` and fail if a genuine posted round is silent, if a missing-context result is silent or double-pinged, or if a no-post failure pings.

**Out of scope**

- Changing the mockup variants, screenshots, selection interaction, or any user-facing surface.
- Replacing or adding retry guarantees to the best-effort notification transport.
- Resolving the sibling marker-conflation problem that makes `MISSING-CONTEXT:` look like a completed round for eligibility purposes.
- Removing or redesigning the existing intake/park notification.

<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

## What's missing

The mockup phase (#29 / #53) now draws variants on a parked `needs-mockup` issue on its own and posts them for the maintainer to pick in one reply. But nothing tells the maintainer the pick is ready.

The "agentflow needs you" ping fires at **park** time — when intake routes the issue to `needs-mockup` — which is *before* anything has been drawn, so there's nothing to look at yet. When the variants are actually drawn and posted (`produce_once`), no notification is sent. The feature's promise is that a UI issue advances by itself up to the single decision only the maintainer can make. If that moment isn't signaled, the issue can sit with variants drawn and ready indefinitely, defeating the point — the queue stalls at exactly the step the notification exists to unblock.

Send an "agentflow needs you" notification when `produce_once` successfully posts the variant round (link to the issue), matching how build/park/review-done notify today. Decide what the failure path should do too: a `MISSING-CONTEXT:` result currently dead-ends silently as well (see the sibling marker-conflation gap) — at minimum it likely warrants its own ping so a stuck mockup issue isn't invisible.

- A drawn variant round produces exactly one notification, pointing at the issue.
- No notification on a session that errored/timed out without posting (that path retries on its own next cycle).
- The park-time `needs-mockup` ping isn't duplicated by the new one.

entries.title: Pool balancing: pace weekly-only Codex dispatch against an 80% weekly allowance
entries.body:
> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

**Summary**

Pace unattended Codex dispatch across a reported weekly-only window, releasing 80% of the allowance linearly through the week while reserving the final 20% for interactive work. Detect windows from their reported durations rather than assuming `primary` means five hours and `secondary` means weekly.

**Verified**

No read-only real-data pull is declared for this repository, so verification used the machine’s read-only Codex session reports and the installed gate.

The latest report at `2026-07-13T23:32:00.468Z` contains exactly one limit: `primary.used_percent = 64`, `window_minutes = 10080`, and `resets_at = 1784566349` (July 20 at 09:52 MST). `secondary` is null. The window began July 13 at 09:52 MST; roughly 400 of 10,080 minutes had elapsed, so an 80%-paced allowance had released only about 3.2%. The observed 64% usage is therefore well ahead of pace and unattended Codex dispatch should pause.

The premise holds in the current implementation. `latest_codex_rate_limits` reads the report correctly, but the gate’s `spend` and `check` branches assign `primary` to the variable representing five-hour usage and print it as `trailing-5h`. The burn branch obtains weekly usage and reset time from the missing `secondary` value, producing 0% weekly usage and an epoch reset. In agentflow, `_query_pool` and `parse_pct` preserve only the resulting percentage and clear/blocked decision, so the balancer cannot recover the actual window shape.

The linked report describes the five-hour removal as temporary. OpenAI’s current guidance also treats plan limits and reset details as live plan-dependent facts rather than a fixed two-window contract. The scheduler must therefore follow the windows Codex reports, including the automatic return of a 300-minute window.

**Current behavior**

At the observed 64%, the weekly window is presented to agentflow as 64% of a trailing five-hour limit. Outside burn mode, that is compared with the ordinary 40% short-window threshold. In the idle burn branch, the absent weekly window can instead manufacture a reset thousands of hours in the past and allow repeated dispatch up to the 85% burn ceiling. Neither branch represents the real weekly-only allowance.

`PoolStatus` contains no window duration or reset time, and `choose_pair` can only compare the collapsed percentage. A missing or unparseable clear response also falls back to 0% spent, which is unsafe for a new limit shape.

**Desired behavior**

For a valid 10,080-minute weekly window, calculate the released unattended allowance as `min(80, 80 × elapsed / 10080)`, using the reported reset to derive the window start. Dispatch Codex only while reported usage is below that released allowance. At the observed point, 64% usage versus about 3.2% released means unavailable.

Treat every reported window independently and require all applicable windows to permit dispatch. Classify the 300-minute and 10,080-minute windows by duration, not by `primary`/`secondary` position. If a 300-minute window returns, its existing short-window policy resumes automatically alongside weekly pacing. In-flight work finishes; pacing gates new sessions and is re-evaluated from fresh facts before subsequent dispatch.

Keep policy in agentflow and facts in the gate, matching the accepted activity-adaptive ceiling decision. Extend the gate’s read-only contract to report every window’s usage, duration, and reset time; do not duplicate Codex transcript scanning inside agentflow.

**Key interfaces**

Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers:

- `PoolStatus`, `_query_pool`, `choose_pair`, and `pick_pair` in the balancer — carry window facts far enough to make the dispatch decision while preserving the single-tool fallback and cross-tool review rules.
- The `triage-gate.sh` adapter — expose structured read-only limit facts backward-compatibly. Its current `spend` text collapses window identity and cannot support this policy. Coordinate the required companion change in the gate’s owning repository before enabling the production path.
- `parse_pct` — retain only as a compatibility path for known legacy output; unknown or weekly-only facts must never degrade to 0% spent and clear.
- `dashboard_data.pools` — preserve raw plan usage/headroom semantics. This issue changes scheduling policy, not the dashboard presentation.
- The accepted pool-balancing and activity-adaptive ceiling decisions — record that Codex windows are dynamic and weekly pacing is an additional dispatch constraint, without re-litigating the 85% idle / 50% active short-window policy.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A fixture with `used_percent = 64`, `window_minutes = 10080`, `resets_at = 1784566349`, and no secondary window is recognized as weekly-only rather than trailing-five-hour usage.
- [ ] At `2026-07-13T23:32:00.468Z`, that fixture computes approximately 3.2% released allowance and blocks unattended Codex dispatch.
- [ ] One quarter through a 10,080-minute window, 19% usage is eligible and 20% usage is not; halfway through, 39% is eligible and 40% is not; immediately before reset, 79% is eligible and 80% is not.
- [ ] Swapping a 300-minute and 10,080-minute window between `primary` and `secondary` produces the same decision.
- [ ] When both windows are reported, both must permit dispatch; restoring the 300-minute window automatically restores the existing short-window constraint.
- [ ] A missing, malformed, or unknown window fact fails closed rather than becoming 0% spent and clear.
- [ ] A missing secondary window never creates an epoch reset, negative time-to-reset message, or false burn eligibility.
- [ ] The gate remains the transcript/rate-limit adapter and reports facts; agentflow owns the 80% pacing formula and dispatch decision.
- [ ] Regression tests exercise the behavior through `pick_pair` and fail if the observed weekly-only fixture can select Codex for a new unattended session.
- [ ] Existing single-pool fallback, cross-tool reviewer selection, operator dispatch behavior, and ordinary 300-minute-window behavior remain covered.

**Out of scope**

- Predicting a session’s future quota cost, killing work already in flight, or purchasing credits.
- Changing the 80% reserve dynamically by task complexity or model tier.
- Implementing headroom-governed concurrency or the separate 85% idle / 50% active ceiling work.
- Redesigning the dashboard or changing its visible pool widget; any later presentation change still requires the locked UI-spec process.
- Scraping Codex session files from a second implementation inside agentflow.

entries.title: Auto-merge: mark draft PRs ready before squash-merge
entries.body:
> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Summary

Make the final auto-merge action ensure a draft PR is ready for review before attempting its squash-merge. Keep the readiness transition inside the merge interface so both autonomous merge paths inherit the behavior.

## Verified

No read-only production-data pull is declared for this repo, so verification used the checked-out pipeline and tests.

`decide_merge` can return `MERGE` without inspecting draft state. Its `MERGE` branch in `_build_review_merge` and the clean-survivor branch in `_merge_autonomous_survivor` both call `squash_merge` directly.

There are exactly **2** production callers of `squash_merge`. The function currently issues exactly **1** GitHub command—`gh pr merge --squash --delete-branch`—and performs **0** draft-state checks or ready-for-review transitions. The premise therefore holds: GitHub can reject an otherwise mergeable draft PR, and agentflow reads that rejection as a generic merge failure.

The `reviewed` and `guarded` branches make **0** pipeline merge attempts; they park the reviewed PR for a human, as required by the autonomy-profile decision.

## Current behavior

After independent review and green CI, an autonomous PR reaches `MergeDecision.MERGE`. Both the initial build path and survivor-recheck path pass it straight to `squash_merge`. A non-draft PR can merge, but a draft PR is sent directly to GitHub's squash-merge command and fails. The initial build path then parks and pings for a generic branch-protection, conflict, or transient failure; the survivor path also parks it.

## Desired behavior

At the moment an autonomous PR has cleared every existing merge gate, determine whether it is still a draft. If it is, mark it ready for review and only then run the existing squash-merge. A failure to inspect or change readiness must fail closed and must not attempt the merge. Already-ready PRs must continue through the normal merge path.

## Key interfaces

Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.

- `agentflow.gate.squash_merge` is the existing merge interface and the natural place to hide draft handling from its callers.
- `_build_review_merge` and `_merge_autonomous_survivor` are the **2** autonomous callers that must retain their existing success and parking behavior.
- Keep `decide_merge` focused on review, CI, independence, UI evidence, and maintainer-reply gates; draft readiness is an execution precondition after those gates pass.
- Do not accidentally mark `_preserve_progress` handback PRs ready: those drafts represent unfinished work and never pass through the merge interface.
- Treat an already-ready PR idempotently, and do not let a failed readiness lookup or transition fall through to `gh pr merge`.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A draft PR that reaches the autonomous merge action is marked ready for review before its squash-merge is attempted.
- [ ] The existing **2** autonomous merge paths receive the behavior through the shared merge interface.
- [ ] An already-ready PR still performs the existing squash-merge without being rejected by readiness handling.
- [ ] If draft state cannot be determined, or marking a draft ready fails, the merge interface returns failure and issues **0** squash-merge commands.
- [ ] Existing parking, notification, and ratchet behavior handles that failure without introducing a second failure path.
- [ ] A test exercises `squash_merge` through its public interface and asserts command ordering for a draft PR: readiness succeeds before squash-merge. This test must fail if the readiness step is removed.
- [ ] Tests cover an already-ready PR and a readiness failure that prevents the merge command.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` passes.

## Out of scope

- Do not change the review, CI, reviewer-independence, UI-evidence, or maintainer-comment gates.
- Do not make `reviewed` or `guarded` repos auto-merge; their human-merge policy remains unchanged.
- Do not mark unfinished handback drafts ready for review.
- Do not change the dashboard or any other user-facing surface.

<!-- agentflow:original-below -->
<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

## What happens

When a build agent opens its PR as a *draft* (some Codex setups do this by default — see ConnorGriffin/home-depot-location-probe#17), the finished, CI-green PR is left in draft state. On an **autonomous** repo the merge step then silently fails: GitHub refuses to merge a draft, so the squash-merge returns failure and the PR gets parked for a reason that has nothing to do with its content or review. The work is good; it just never lands.

On a **reviewed** repo it's milder — the human reviewer has to click "Ready for review" by hand before GitHub will let them merge.

## Why it matters

The pipeline treats "agent opened a PR" as the success signal, but doesn't account for the PR being a draft. A draft is a normal, correct thing for a build agent to produce — the merge machinery should handle it rather than stalling on it.

## What to check

When the pipeline is about to merge a PR, it should first ensure the PR is out of draft state (mark it ready for review), then proceed with the squash-merge. After the fix: a green draft PR on an autonomous repo should auto-merge the same as a non-draft one.

</details>

entries.title: Build dispatch: skip ready issues with open blockers
entries.body:
> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Agent Brief

### Summary

Make build dispatch honor same-repository `Blocked by #N` declarations. A ready issue must remain eligible for intake but must not start building while any declared blocker is open or its state cannot be determined.

### Verified

- `_next_ready_issue` currently requests up to 50 open `ready-for-agent` issues with `number`, `title`, `body`, and `labels`, then sorts eligible candidates by issue number.
- `_free_to_dispatch` applies exactly 2 ownership checks: the issue has no open agentflow PR and lacks the `agentflow:building` claim. It never reads `body`; there are currently 0 dependency-state checks.
- The existing `_next_ready_issue` test covers failure to retrieve in-flight work and then confirms issue #5 is selected. No dispatch-interface test covers an open or closed blocker.
- `apply_intake` already routes ready issues through `compose_ready_body`, which preserves the original description verbatim beneath `<!-- agentflow:original-below -->`. A `Blocked by #N` declaration therefore survives today, but that contract is not explicitly tested.
- The accepted dependency-dispatch decision still mentions filtering build and triage. This issue explicitly resolves that wording in favor of build-only gating; the decision record should be aligned while intake remains unchanged.
- This repository declares no grounding fetch, so verification is code-based rather than against external data.

### Current behavior

The daemon examines at most 50 ready candidates and chooses the lowest-numbered candidate that is neither claimed nor represented by an open agentflow PR. A ready issue #42 containing `Blocked by #41` is eligible even while #41 is open because its body is fetched but ignored.

### Desired behavior

Recognize one or more exact `Blocked by #N` declarations in a ready issue's body and recompute their same-repository issue states during every build-selection pass. Skip the dependent when any blocker is open or cannot be checked safely; log the dependent and blocker so the wait is visible. Once every blocker is closed, select the issue normally on the next cycle. Do not introduce a release event, stored dependency state, or intake gate.

### Key interfaces

Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.

- `_next_ready_issue` is the daemon's ready-queue selection interface. It already has candidate bodies and must incorporate blocker state before returning the oldest eligible issue.
- `_free_to_dispatch` is shared by daemon selection and the by-hand `build_issue` path. Preserve one build eligibility rule so manual build cannot bypass an open blocker.
- The cycle logger currently reaches `run_once` but not `_next_ready_issue`; carry enough logging context into selection to report blocker skips without weakening the fail-closed behavior.
- `compose_ready_body` is the intake durability boundary. Preserve its idempotent original-body behavior and explicitly lock down `Blocked by` survival.
- Parse declarations as dependency metadata, not incidental prose. Multiple declarations mean all blockers must be closed.
- Keep dependency checks distinct from the existing claim/open-PR checks; an inability to determine blocker state must skip the dependent rather than become an empty blocker set.

### Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Given ready issue #42 with `Blocked by #41`, where #41 is open, `_next_ready_issue` does not return #42.
- [ ] If ready issue #43 has no dependency while #42 is blocked by open #41, selection returns #43 and logs that #42 was skipped for #41.
- [ ] After #41 closes, the next selection pass can return the same issue #42 without any release event or stored transition.
- [ ] With `Blocked by #40` and `Blocked by #41`, issue #42 remains skipped while either blocker is open and becomes eligible only after both are closed.
- [ ] If the state of #41 cannot be determined, issue #42 fails closed and is not dispatched.
- [ ] A ready issue with no `Blocked by` declaration follows the existing behavior, including the 50-candidate cap, lowest-number ordering, claim check, and open-PR check.
- [ ] The by-hand build interface refuses the same open-blocker case rather than bypassing the ready-queue gate.
- [ ] Intake still grounds blocked issues normally; only build dispatch is gated.
- [ ] A test through `compose_ready_body` proves an original `Blocked by #41` declaration remains in the rewritten issue body and is visible to dispatch.
- [ ] The dependency decision record describes build-only gating consistently with the implemented behavior.
- [ ] Tests exercise `_next_ready_issue` / `_free_to_dispatch` so removing the dependency gate makes the open-#41 case fail.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` passes.

### Out of scope

- A dashboard blocked chip or any other user-facing surface.
- GitHub sub-issues, task-list dependencies, cross-repository blockers, or a general dependency graph.
- Cycle detection, automatic blocker repair, release events, or dependency state stored outside GitHub.
- Preventing intake/grounding of blocked issues.
- Changing ready-queue ordering, the 50-candidate limit, dispatch claims, open-PR deduplication, or concurrent fan-out.

<!-- agentflow:original-below -->
<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

Implements [ADR 0024](docs/adr/0024-dependency-aware-dispatch.md).

## Problem

Build dispatch picks the oldest `ready-for-agent` issue with no notion of dependencies (`_next_ready_issue` → `_free_to_dispatch` in `agentflow/loop.py`). So an ordered chain of slices (e.g. the M6 dashboard re-platform) can't be filed as a batch — a later slice may build before the one it depends on has merged. The only workaround today is filing one issue at a time.

## What to build

Teach build dispatch to respect a `Blocked by #N` declaration in the issue body:

- Parse one or more `Blocked by #N` references from an issue body.
- In the build-side selection, treat a ready issue as **not dispatchable while any of its blockers is still open**. `_next_ready_issue` already fetches the issue `body`, so the data is there.
- **Recompute each cycle — no release event.** When the last blocker closes (its PR merges), the dependent becomes dispatchable on the next pass. This preserves the daemon's stateless/crash-safe property (ADR 0011).
- **Gate the build side, not triage.** A blocked issue should still be triaged/grounded by intake up front so it's ready the moment it unblocks. (This refines ADR 0024's phrasing that mentioned triage — the load-bearing gate is build dispatch.)
- **Fail safe:** a dependency cycle or a never-closing blocker just means the dependents never dispatch — never a wrong build. Log when an issue is skipped for an open blocker so it's visible.
- The `Blocked by #N` declaration **must survive intake's body rewrite** (intake rewrites title/description) — preserve the line into the Agent Brief, or otherwise track it durably.

## Acceptance

- A `ready-for-agent` issue with an open `Blocked by #N` is **not** selected by `_next_ready_issue`.
- Once #N closes, the same issue **is** selected on the next cycle.
- An issue with no `Blocked by` line dispatches exactly as today.
- Tested **through the dispatch interface** (not just a parse helper) — the real bug lives in selection, so the test exercises `_next_ready_issue` / `_free_to_dispatch`: a blocked issue is skipped, an unblocked one is picked.

## Pointers

- `agentflow/loop.py` — `_free_to_dispatch` (~258), `_next_ready_issue` (~266).
- ADR 0024 for rationale; ADR 0021 (dispatch dedup) for the adjacent claim mechanism.

</details>

> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

**Summary**

Build the first dashboard-v2 vertical slice: a FastAPI server exposing the existing snapshot contract behind a roughly 15-second cache, plus a Vite/Svelte console shell whose Inbox is bound to that contract. Keep the stdlib dashboard operational while the new stack proves the end-to-end path.

**Verified**

- `agentflow.dashboard_data.snapshot()` currently returns `dispatch`, `pools`, and `repos`; it does not yet return the proposed v2 `daemon`, `running`, `held`, `parked`, `stage`, or `checks` fields.
- `agentflow.server.Handler.do_GET` invokes `snapshot()` for every `/api/snapshot` request, so there is currently no server-side cache.
- The existing browser polls every `15` seconds. Its `deriveInbox()` includes every in-flight PR from `reviewed` or `guarded` repos, excludes autonomous in-flight PRs, adds repos whose ratchet is ready to loosen, and orders guarded merges before reviewed merges before ratchet prompts with weights `1`, `2`, and `3`.
- The locked mockup is present in both required files: `mockups/dashboard-v2-combined.html` and `.js`. Its v2 derivation cannot be lifted unchanged in this slice because it filters on `stage` and `checks`, fields absent from today's snapshot.
- The repository currently has `0` FastAPI dependencies, `0` JavaScript package manifests or lockfiles, `0` Svelte source files, and `1` shipped stdlib dashboard HTML file. The requested stack is not already implemented.
- A read-only snapshot run over the `6` configured repos returned `2` pools, `2` ready issues, `0` in-flight PRs, `38` recent-merge entries, and an Inbox count of `0`. Dispatch was enabled; Claude had `66%` headroom and Codex had `100%` headroom.

**Current behavior**

The daemon and `uv run python -m agentflow.server` serve the existing static dashboard through the stdlib server. Each browser refresh causes a fresh snapshot round over GitHub. With today's real snapshot, the Inbox is empty because there are `0` in-flight PRs and no ratchet-ready prompt.

**Desired behavior**

A documented `uv run` target starts a FastAPI app that serves the unchanged current snapshot shape and the built Svelte SPA. The SPA polls every `3–5` seconds, while the server allows at most one GitHub-backed snapshot refresh per roughly `15` seconds. The app lands on the locked-spec Inbox, preserves today's derivation and urgency order, exposes the four-tab console shell and keyboard navigation, and leaves the other three views and drill-down as explicit stubs.

**Key interfaces**

Explore fresh; these are pointers, not line numbers:

- `agentflow/dashboard_data.py`: retain `snapshot()` as the source of truth rather than duplicating GitHub shaping in the web layer.
- `agentflow/server.py` and its daemon ownership in `agentflow/daemon.py`: the old stdlib server and its lifecycle must continue working unchanged until parity is reached.
- The new FastAPI app: own built-asset serving, `/api/snapshot`, and the TTL cache behind one small public interface. A fast concurrent burst must be single-flight, not merely several simultaneous cache misses.
- `agentflow/static/dashboard.html`: authoritative description of today's snapshot contract and Inbox derivation.
- `mockups/dashboard-v2-combined.html` and `.js`: locked shell, tab bar, Inbox rows, keyboard behavior, tokens, and accessibility guidance. Do not copy the proposed-v2 `stage`/`checks` filter into this current-contract slice.
- `PRODUCT.md` and `DESIGN.md`: preserve the terminal-native density, semantic colors, rows-over-cards rule, reduced-motion behavior, and prohibition on side-stripe accents.
- `AGENTS.md`: extend `ui-surfaces:` with the chosen Svelte source location so future UI changes trigger screenshot review.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] A documented `uv run` command starts the new FastAPI server, serves the built SPA, and returns HTTP `200` from `/api/snapshot`.
- [ ] `/api/snapshot` preserves the current `dispatch` + `pools` + `repos` payload contract produced by `dashboard_data.snapshot()`.
- [ ] The server caches that GitHub-backed result for approximately `15` seconds; an interface-level test sends a burst of requests and proves they invoke `snapshot()` exactly `1` time, then proves a request after expiry refreshes it.
- [ ] The browser polls `/api/snapshot` every `3–5` seconds without multiplying GitHub calls inside the cache window.
- [ ] The Svelte app implements the locked console shell with Inbox, Live, Fleet, and History tabs; Inbox is the default and the other `3` views are clearly empty stubs.
- [ ] Tab semantics, visible focus, `1–4` tab switching, and Inbox `j`/`k` navigation match the locked spec. Any drill-down behavior introduced in this slice may be a stub; controls remain non-mutating.
- [ ] Inbox rendering preserves today's public behavior: guarded in-flight rows rank first, reviewed in-flight rows second, ratchet-ready rows third, and autonomous in-flight rows never appear. A frontend test fails if that ordering or exclusion regresses.
- [ ] Inbox-zero renders correctly for the grounded current case of `0` in-flight PRs and `0` derived Inbox items.
- [ ] Before/after screenshots at the same viewport compare the locked Inbox spec with the implemented SPA and are attached as UI evidence.
- [ ] `AGENTS.md` lists the new frontend source prefix under `ui-surfaces:`.
- [ ] The existing `agentflow.server` dashboard, `agentflow/static/dashboard.html`, and daemon-owned dashboard lifecycle remain operational.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` passes, and the frontend build and its focused tests pass from a clean checkout.

**Out of scope**

- Do not add held or parked rows, daemon live-session state, the proposed v2 snapshot fields, or populated Live/Fleet/History views.
- Do not add POST controls, authentication, merge/loosen/pause/pickup behavior, or any GitHub mutation.
- Do not change dispatch concurrency.
- Do not retire, redirect, or rewrite the existing stdlib server or dashboard.

First slice of the M6 dashboard re-platform ([ADR 0023](docs/adr/0023-dashboard-replatform-control-plane.md), ROADMAP M6). Proves the new stack end-to-end; later slices thicken it.

entries.title: Live board: daemon writes a live-session state file; snapshot exposes running[] + a daemon block
entries.body:
*agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

> Blocked by #69 (the FastAPI + Svelte shell this builds on). Concurrency is a *later* slice — see Out of scope.

## Summary

The daemon is the only process that knows which agents are executing right now. Surface that: the daemon writes a live-session state file as sessions start and finish, the API merges it into the fleet snapshot as a top-level `running[]` list plus a `daemon` status block, and the console gains the **Live** tab — triaging → building → reviewing lanes — exactly as the locked spec already draws it.

## Verified (against this checkout)

- **The tracking already exists; it just isn't surfaced.** Every spawned session — build, review, triage, and revise — is wrapped by the *same* `worktree_session(...)` context manager, and the child agent's PID is persisted to a per-worktree `agentflow-active` marker as the session runs. Liveness (`is this PID alive`), active-session detection, and startup reaping of dead sessions are all already implemented and used by the daemon's crash-recovery pass. **None of it reaches the operator** — the fleet snapshot today returns only dispatch/pools/repos, with no notion of a running session.
- **The contract is locked, not open.** The locked visual spec pins an exact per-session shape: `repo, number, title, stage (triaging|building|reviewing), tool, model, branch, worktree, pid, started_at`, plus a `daemon` block of `enabled, last_cycle_at, poll_seconds` and a gh-cache-freshness timestamp. This build fills that contract; it does not design it.
- **Serial dispatch is still in force.** The fleet still runs one session at a time (dropping that cap is a separate, later slice). So with a real build in flight the Live board shows **exactly one** session; at rest it shows **zero**. The multi-session, all-lanes-full picture in the mockup's sample data is illustrative of the *later* concurrent world — do not fake it to fill the lanes.

## Current behavior

- The state file does not exist. Nothing outside the daemon process can see a running session.
- The snapshot has no `running[]` and no `daemon` block. The console has no Live view.
- On daemon startup, stale worktrees from a crashed run are already reaped; there is simply no session file for a parallel reaping step to clean.

## Desired behavior

- As each session starts, the daemon records one live-session entry (all ten fields above) in a JSON state file under the agentflow state dir; as the session finishes, that entry is removed. If the daemon crashes and restarts, entries whose owning process is no longer alive are dropped (reusing the liveness signal the recovery pass already trusts) — no dead session ever lingers in the file.
- The API reads that file and merges it into the fleet snapshot: a top-level `running[]` and a `daemon` block (enabled / last cycle time / poll interval / how fresh the cached GitHub reads are). Per-pool running counts are derived from `running[]` so the Live correlation strip stays honest.
- The **Live** tab renders per the locked spec: triaging → building → reviewing lanes, compact session rows, **per-stage counts always visible** (`0 · 0 · 0 — fleet idle` when quiet), a per-pool running-count + headroom correlation strip, and elapsed time ticking up from each session's `started_at`.

## Key interfaces (explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers)

- **The write seam is already unified.** One context manager wraps every session type (build / review / triage / revise) — that is the natural single place to write the entry on entry and remove it on exit. It currently only knows the worktree path, so it needs the session descriptor (number, title, stage, tool, model, branch, pid, started_at) threaded through from each call site. **Trap:** don't scatter the write across four call sites when the shared wrapper already spans all of them — one seam, all stages. **Trap:** `stage` is per-call-site (triage→triaging, build/revise→building, review→reviewing); it is not derivable from the worktree alone.
- **Reaping already has a home.** The startup worktree-recovery pass is where a dead-session sweep of the state file belongs — reuse the existing PID/marker liveness, don't invent a second notion of "alive." **Trap:** the active-marker briefly holds the daemon's own PID before the child PID overwrites it; use the same liveness check the recovery pass already trusts rather than rolling your own.
- **The snapshot merge** belongs where both the reader and the shape live — coordinate with #69's FastAPI server. The `daemon` block's `last_cycle_at` and gh-cache-freshness are runtime facts the server/daemon hold, not values the current snapshot builder receives — they must be threaded in. **Trap:** the state file is written by the daemon but read by the server; treat a missing/partial/corrupt file as "fleet idle" (empty `running[]`), never a 500.
- **Model display:** the runner resolves complexity → a concrete model string (e.g. `opus`/`sonnet` and the codex model ids); the spec shows the short form (`opus`, `sol`, `sonnet`). Store or shorten so the row matches the lock.
- **The Live tab render helpers are pre-written** in the locked spec's `.js` (the kanban, per-stage counts, correlation strip, ticking `elapsed`) — lift them, don't reinvent.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] With a real build in flight, the state file holds exactly that one session with all ten fields populated (`stage:building`, real `pid`, `started_at`); the API's `running[]` exposes it. When the session ends, the entry disappears from both.
- [ ] A session whose owning process is dead is dropped from the file on daemon startup — it never appears in `running[]`.
- [ ] The API also returns a `daemon` block: `enabled`, `last_cycle_at`, `poll_seconds`, and a gh-cache-freshness timestamp.
- [ ] Per-pool running counts in the snapshot are derived from `running[]` (not tracked separately), so a pool's count always equals its sessions in the list.
- [ ] **Live tab at idle:** lanes render with `0 · 0 · 0 — fleet idle`; no crash on empty/missing state file.
- [ ] **Live tab with one session:** the row lands in the correct lane, elapsed ticks up from `started_at`, and the correlation strip shows the pool's running count against its headroom. Screenshot both states against the locked spec (charter before/after gate).
- [ ] **Regression test through the interface:** the daemon writes an entry on session start and removes it on finish; the snapshot merges it into `running[]`; and a state file seeded with a dead-PID entry has that entry dropped after the startup reap. A test that would have passed before this change (dead entry survives, or `running[]` absent) is the one that must now fail.

## Out of scope (explicit don'ts)

- **Do not drop the serial-dispatch cap / add concurrency.** That is a separate later slice; here the Live board is correct with 0 or 1 session. Don't fake multiple sessions to populate the lanes.
- **No control actions / POST verbs** (pause, loosen, merge, pickup) — a later slice.
- **No other tabs** — Fleet, History, and the held/parked inbox rows are not this slice.
- **No SQLite / durable history** — a JSON state file is the decided mechanism.
- **Don't touch the retiring stdlib dashboard** beyond what the snapshot-shape change forces; the new surface is the FastAPI/Svelte app from #69.

<!-- agentflow:original-below -->
<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

Blocked by #69

M6 slice 2 ([ADR 0023](docs/adr/0023-dashboard-replatform-control-plane.md)). The daemon is the only process that knows what agents are executing right now (it already tracks child PIDs + worktree markers — `runner.py`); surface that.

## What to build

- The **daemon writes a live-session state file** (JSON under `~/.agentflow/`) as sessions start/finish: one entry per running session with `repo, number, title, stage (triaging|building|reviewing), tool, model, branch, worktree, pid, started_at` — the `running[]` contract the locked mockup binds (see `mockups/dashboard-v2-combined.js`). Stale entries (dead PIDs) must not linger; recover on daemon startup.
- The FastAPI server merges the state file into `/api/snapshot` as top-level `running[]` + a `daemon` block (`enabled, last_cycle_at, poll_seconds`, gh-cache freshness).
- The **Live tab** per the locked spec: triaging → building → reviewing lanes, compact session rows, per-stage counts always visible ("0 · 0 · 0 — fleet idle" when quiet), per-pool running-count + headroom correlation strip, elapsed ticking from `started_at`.

## Acceptance

- With a build in flight, the state file holds the session and `/api/snapshot` exposes it; when the session ends (or its PID dies), it disappears.
- Live tab matches the locked spec at idle and with sessions (screenshot gate).
- State-file write/read covered through the interface (daemon writes on spawn/finish; snapshot merges; a dead-PID entry is dropped).

</details>

> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Summary

Dashboard v2, slice 3 of the re-platform ([ADR 0023](docs/adr/0023-dashboard-replatform-control-plane.md)). Complete the needs-you inbox — today it silently omits **held issues** and **parked PRs** — and land the two remaining read surfaces (**Fleet** and **History**) against the already-locked visual spec. - **Held/parked are genuinely missing today.** `dashboard_data.snapshot()` / `repo_view()` return only `ready` / `in_flight` / `recent_merges` / `ratchet` — no `held[]`, no `parked[]`. So held issues (`agentflow:needs-grilling`, `agentflow:needs-mockup`) and parked PRs never reach the inbox, exactly as filed.

  - `ui-evidence` — park body contains the UI-gap reason (`loop._UI_GAP_REASON`, wired at `loop.py` PARK/merge paths).
  - `failed-merge` — the squash-merge-failed park reason ("could not be squash-merged…") or the conflict-survivor marker (`loop._CONFLICT_MARK`, "conflicts after main advanced").
  - `open-question` — the PR has an unanswered maintainer question, i.e. `gate.reply_pending()` is true.
  - `drop-to-reviewed` — the normal `reviewed`/`guarded` hand-off park ("is a `{profile}` repo — a human merges" / "could not be auto-merged after review").
  Every park comment starts with the `> *agentflow: parked for human review.*` marker (or the conflict marker), so parked PRs are found by scanning agentflow PR comments for those markers, then classified into one reason.
- **The snapshot contract is pinned by the locked mockup** (`dashboard-v2-combined.js` header, lines 12–17): `repos[]` gains `held[]` and `parked[]`; held rows carry `{number, title, state, reason, since}`, parked rows carry `{number, title, reason, builder, reviewer, since}`. Inbox ordering, Fleet columns, and the History feed are all rendered there — port them, don't redesign.

## Current behavior

The inbox derives only from in-flight PRs + ratchet-ready. Held issues and parked PRs are invisible. Fleet and History tabs do not exist (the v2 shell from slice 1 leaves `#view-fleet` / `#view-history` as empty panels).

## Desired behavior

- The v2 `/api/snapshot` per-repo payload gains `held[]` and `parked[]` (shapes above) and carries `effort` alongside `complexity` on ready issues.
- **Inbox** shows held rows (Reply / Mock up actions per the held state) and parked rows (per-reason primary action per the spec's PARK map: Review drop / Retry merge / Answer / Add proof), ranked most-urgent-first exactly as the locked spec derives (parked outranks held; held `needs-grilling` outranks `needs-mockup`; oldest-first within a weight).
- **Fleet tab**: the repo × signals master table with per-repo held/parked counts and expand-in-place lanes, per the locked spec.
- **History tab**: the flattened reverse-chronological merged feed, per the locked spec.
- Held/parked entries disappear from the snapshot and inbox once resolved (label removed / PR merged or closed).

## Key interfaces (explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers)

- **Snapshot derivation** — `agentflow/dashboard_data.py` (`repo_view`, `snapshot`, and the `gh`-query helpers `_ready_issues` / `_prs`, plus `_effort_of`). Add held-issue and parked-PR derivation here as pure-shaping-over-`gh` in the same read-*over*-GitHub style. **Trap:** slice 1 re-platforms this to FastAPI; build on that slice's snapshot module/contract, not the v1 stdlib one — coordinate with where slice 1 lands the v2 `snapshot()`.
- **Park markers** — `agentflow/loop.py` (`_UI_GAP_REASON`, `_CONFLICT_MARK`, the PARK / merge-failed branches) and `agentflow/gate.py` (`park`, `reply_pending`). Read these to build the reason classifier; keep the classifier a small pure function so it's testable through the interface. **Trap:** don't re-derive park state by re-running pipeline logic — read the posted markers/labels that already exist.
- **Held labels** — `agentflow:needs-grilling` / `agentflow:needs-mockup` (`loop.HELD_LABELS`, `intake.STATE_LABELS`); `since` from the label/issue timing.
- **Frontend** — the Svelte views from slices 1–2. Port the rendering verbatim from `mockups/dashboard-v2-combined.js` (`heldRow`, `parkedRow`, inbox ordering, Fleet `FLEET_COLS`/accessors, History flattening) and `.html` (Fleet/History panels, `k-held`/`k-parked` styling). This is a read surface: no write actions in this slice (controls are a later slice).

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `/api/snapshot` per-repo payload includes `held[]` (`{number, title, state, reason, since}`) and `parked[]` (`{number, title, reason ∈ {drop-to-reviewed, failed-merge, open-question, ui-evidence}, builder, reviewer, since}`), and `effort` appears alongside `complexity` on ready issues.
- [ ] A held issue (labeled `needs-grilling` or `needs-mockup`) and a parked PR appear in `/api/snapshot` and in the Inbox with the correct kind, reason, and age; both leave the snapshot and inbox once resolved (label removed / PR merged or closed).
- [ ] Parked-reason classification is correct for all four markers: UI-gap → `ui-evidence`; squash-merge-fail / conflict-survivor → `failed-merge`; unanswered maintainer question (`reply_pending`) → `open-question`; normal reviewed/guarded hand-off → `drop-to-reviewed`.
- [ ] Inbox ordering matches the locked spec (parked > held, `needs-grilling` > `needs-mockup`, oldest-first within a weight).
- [ ] Fleet and History tabs render and match the locked spec — **before/after headless-Playwright screenshots attached** as proof-of-match (blocking without them).
- [ ] A test exercises the derivation through the interface: given a repo with a held issue, a parked PR (each of the four reasons), and ready issues, the snapshot arrays and inbox ordering come out correct — and it fails if held/parked are dropped or misclassified.

## Out of scope

- **No write actions / controls** — the inbox and per-reason buttons render, but wiring them to POST verbs is a later slice.
- **No Live tab / live-session state** — that is slice 2.
- **No changes to the pipeline's park/hold behavior** — read the markers it already writes; don't add or rename them.
- **No visual redesign** — match `mockups/dashboard-v2-combined.*`; any deviation needs `/ui-mockups` first.
- **No SQLite / durable history store** — History reads from the live snapshot; the durable store is explicitly deferred (ADR 0023).

entries.title: dispatch: headroom-governed concurrent builds with an activity-adaptive spend ceiling
entries.body:
M6 slice 5 — independent of the dashboard slices. Implements the dispatch half of [ADR 0023](docs/adr/0023-dashboard-replatform-control-plane.md) and [ADR 0025](docs/adr/0025-activity-adaptive-spend-ceiling.md).

## What to build

- **Drop the one-issue-per-repo-per-cycle serialization** (amends ADR 0006): the daemon dispatches ready work concurrently, governed by pool headroom, a machine ceiling (max concurrent sessions, named config), and dedup claims (ADR 0021, already per-issue). **Merges stay serialized** (ADR 0009 collision floor).
- **Concurrency covers every session kind, not just builds** — triage/grounding sessions, builds, reviews, mockup draws. Per-stage concurrency knobs (named config), with **triage allowed higher parallelism than builds**: grounding sessions are shorter and cheaper, and a deep intake queue should drain fast (several triages at once while builds are capacity-bound). The `agentflow:triaging` claim already dedups per-issue.
- **Activity-adaptive ceiling** (ADR 0025): the gate reports facts (trailing-5h spend; operator active/idle — `triage-gate.sh` may need a small companion change in dotfiles to expose activity as a fact; until then, derive from existing `check` behavior and fail toward idle-ceiling), and the **balancer applies policy** as named config: `IDLE_CEILING_PCT=85`, `ACTIVE_CEILING_PCT=50`, pace = 1 new session/cycle per active pool. Operator-active never hard-stops dispatch anymore; it lowers the ceiling and paces. `AGENTFLOW_WT_MARK` exclusion (fleet ≠ operator) is load-bearing — keep it.
- Log dispatch decisions ("claude yielding to operator · ceiling 50%") so the behavior is observable before the dashboard surfaces it.
- Note: the claim-reclaim rules (#74) assume "top of cycle = nothing live" — concurrency breaks that; reclaim must key on real session evidence (live PIDs / the state file) instead.

## Acceptance

- With multiple ready issues across repos and both pools clear, more than one build runs concurrently; several triages run concurrently when the intake queue is deep; total sessions never exceed the machine ceiling; merges never overlap.
- With simulated operator activity on one pool: that pool stops dispatching above 50% spent and paces to one new session per cycle, while the other pool runs at the idle ceiling.
- Covered through the dispatch interface (the ceiling/pacing/concurrency decisions, not just helpers).

entries.title: Codex pacing: refresh stale limit facts before deferring dispatch
entries.body:
> *agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

**Summary**

Actively refresh stale Codex limit facts when they are the only reason that pool cannot dispatch, then re-evaluate the pool once. Persist a cooldown so an exhausted pool receives at most one probe per configured window.

**Verified**

- The dotfiles gate's `latest_codex_rate_limits()` scans Codex transcripts and selects the newest `token_count` event containing `rate_limits`. Its `limits` branch returns only `windows`; it discards the event timestamp even though the scanner already has it.
- Agentflow's `_query_pool()` reads those passive facts. `_codex_dispatch_status()` applies weekly pacing and stale-window checks, while `pick_pair()` only queries, classifies, and chooses runners. There is no active refresh branch.
- `CodexRunner.launch()` runs only after Codex has already been selected. Therefore a blocked Codex pool cannot create the session that would update its own facts.
- Real transcripts show the reported weekly window at 80% through `2026-07-14T01:25:13.700Z`, with reset `1784566349`. At that instant only 4.07% had been released for unattended work, so the existing `used_percent >= released` branch correctly blocked dispatch.
- The first post-reset fact appeared at `2026-07-14T02:31:11.699Z`: 0% with a new reset of `1784601070`. The passive record changed only after a 3,958-second gap containing an externally-started Codex session.
- A read-only live check at `2026-07-14T04:51:32Z` returned one 10,080-minute window at 1%, reset `1784601071`; 1.11% was released, so Codex was eligible again. The gate reported `clear: no trailing-5h window reported`.
- One detail in the filed report differs from the current branch: after the recorded reset passes, `_codex_pacing()` reports `10080-minute limit facts are stale`; it does not become `limit facts unavailable`. The pool still remains blocked indefinitely, so the lockout premise holds.
- This repo declares no read-only real-data pull. The live gate and transcript checks above were read-only.

**Current behavior**

The 80% weekly fact would remain above the release curve for the rest of its recorded window, ending `2026-07-20T16:52:29Z`. After that instant the same fact fails the temporal check as stale. Because every build, review, intake, and mockup reaches Codex through `pick_pair()`, none can run to replace the stale record. An external reset is therefore invisible until an operator starts Codex independently.

**Desired behavior**

Expose when the latest Codex limit fact was observed. For unattended dispatch, when Codex is blocked solely by weekly pacing or temporal staleness and that observation is at least the configured refresh age, run one minimal Codex probe from an agentflow-marked working directory, reload the facts once, and make the dispatch decision from the refreshed result.

Use a default refresh/cooldown window of 21,600 seconds (6 hours), configurable without code changes. Record an attempt before launching it so failures are also bounded. Fresh facts, operator-activity blocks, and independent short-window or malformed-fact blocks must not trigger a probe. A probe must never call `pick_pair()` recursively.

**Key interfaces**

Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.

- The dotfiles limit-fact adapter — retain the latest event's observation timestamp in the structured `limits` contract. This companion adapter change is part of the slice; agentflow must not duplicate transcript scanning.
- `RateLimitWindow` / `PoolStatus` and the Codex fact parser — carry freshness and a structured dispatch-block cause without parsing human-readable reason strings.
- `_codex_dispatch_status()` and `pick_pair()` — distinguish a refreshable pacing/staleness block from activity, short-window capacity, and invalid facts; re-query at most once after a probe.
- The Codex CLI adapter — provide a cheap probe that only needs to produce a rate-limit event. Its cwd must contain the existing `/.agentflow/worktrees/` marker convention so the gate cannot classify it as operator activity.
- Agentflow's persistent state — retain the last probe-attempt time across cycles and daemon restarts, with safe handling of absent or malformed state.
- Issue #73 is already queued to reshape the balancer around activity-adaptive concurrency. Preserve that facts-versus-policy seam and rebase against its eventual shape rather than adding a parallel scheduler.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The structured Codex limit response includes a validated observation timestamp while preserving the existing 300- and 10,080-minute window validation.
- [ ] `AGENTFLOW_CODEX_LIMIT_REFRESH_SECONDS` defaults to 21,600 seconds and controls both stale-age eligibility and the minimum interval between probe attempts.
- [ ] A regression test starts with the observed 80% weekly fact, only 4.1% released, and an observation at least 21,600 seconds old; the probe returns 0% with reset `1784601071`, the facts are re-read exactly once, and Codex becomes dispatchable without operator action.
- [ ] With the same stale 80% result after probing, repeated pool checks during the next 21,599 seconds launch no additional probe and Codex remains blocked. A new attempt may occur once the full 21,600 seconds has elapsed.
- [ ] A blocking fact only 21,599 seconds old does not launch a probe.
- [ ] Operator activity, an independently exhausted 300-minute window, and malformed or unknown facts remain fail-closed and do not launch a probe.
- [ ] A failed or timed-out probe is still recorded as an attempt, remains bounded by the cooldown, and leaves Codex blocked.
- [ ] The probe's session metadata carries a cwd under `/.agentflow/worktrees/`; a gate-level test proves it is excluded from operator activity.
- [ ] The refresh path cannot invoke itself recursively and performs no build, review, GitHub mutation, worktree branch, or operator-facing session work.
- [ ] Existing weekly pacing, operator dispatch, fail-closed parsing, and pool-selection tests remain green under `uv run pytest -q`.

**Out of scope**

- Changing the 80% weekly release curve or deciding whether operator spend counts against it; that intent question belongs to issue #76.
- Implementing issue #73's concurrent dispatch or activity-adaptive 85%/50% ceilings.
- Adding dashboard UI or notifications for refresh attempts.
- Polling Codex continuously or maintaining a long-lived health session.
- Weakening fail-closed handling for malformed, unknown-duration, or temporally impossible limit facts.

<!-- agentflow:original-below -->
<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

## Problem

Codex rate-limit facts are learned passively: the gate scans codex session transcripts for the latest `token_count` → `rate_limits` event (`latest_codex_rate_limits` in dotfiles' triage-gate.sh). Nothing ever queries codex live. So when the operator resets/upgrades their codex limits externally, the newest on-disk fact still shows the pre-reset window, and the pacing gate keeps deferring — and because the fleet never dispatches codex, no session ever writes a fresh fact. A self-sustaining lockout: no dispatch → no fresh facts → no dispatch.

Observed live today: operator reset codex to 100% available; the gate kept reporting "weekly spend at 80%" and the balancer deferred every cycle. Unstuck by hand-running a minimal `codex exec` (8k tokens), after which facts read 0% and dispatch resumed. The stale fact would otherwise have blocked codex until its recorded `resets_at` passed (up to a week), after which it degrades to "limit facts unavailable" — still blocked, forever.

## What to build

A cheap active refresh when passive facts would block: if the codex pool is only blocked by pacing/stale facts AND the newest fact is older than some threshold (config, e.g. 6h), the daemon runs a minimal marked codex session (the `AGENTFLOW_WT_MARK` convention, so it never reads as operator activity) purely to land fresh `rate_limits`, then re-evaluates. Bound it (at most once per threshold window) so a genuinely-limited pool doesn't get pinged in a loop.

## Acceptance

- With stale blocking facts and a genuinely-reset pool, the fleet recovers codex within one refresh threshold without human action.
- With genuinely-exhausted limits, the refresh runs at most once per threshold and the pool stays correctly blocked.
- The refresh session never counts as operator activity and never triggers itself recursively.

</details>

entries.title: agentflow:triaging label: claim description asserts an active grounding session that may not exist
entries.body:
*agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Summary
The `agentflow:triaging` GitHub claim is an ownership marker applied at Intake submission, before admission. Its label description reads *"A grounding session is triaging this issue"* — an assertion of live execution. But the claim is applied while the durable record is `waiting`, and that record can sit queued for capacity (~50 min in the report) with zero attempts and no provider process. The description overclaims. Make it truthful for both queued and running states: an ownership/admission claim, not proof of a live session.

## Verified
Against the real dispatch path:
- **Claim is applied pre-admission, on a `waiting` record.** `dispatch._submit_coordinated_intake` calls `coordinator.submit_stage(submission)` and then `loop._claim_triage(...)` in the same pass (`dispatch.py`, ~line 109). Submission creates the record in state `waiting`; nothing in that pass admits it.
- **The description asserts execution.** `loop._claim_triage` runs `gh label create agentflow:triaging ... --description "A grounding session is triaging this issue"` (`loop.py`, ~line 434-435).
- **A saturated pool keeps the record `waiting`, durably.** Intake reserves 1 permit (`admission.py` row `("intake","claude","opus","deep",None): 1`). `store.reserve` refuses when `SUM(demand) + demand > 5` (`store.py`, ~line 367); `coordinator._begin_start` then reverts state to `waiting` with nothing written (~line 372). So a Build-saturated pool leaves the Intake record `waiting`, no attempt consumed, no family.
- **The Live-view half of the premise does NOT hold — do not "fix" it.** `tracer.live_projection` renders only `state == RUNNING` records; waiting records are omitted by construction (`tracer.py`, ~line 87-94). A blocked Intake record is `waiting`, so it never enters `snap.running`, never gets a `started_at`, and never shows an elapsed timer (`Live.svelte`, ~line 85). The console already presents queued Intake truthfully (by omission). This ticket is the label description only.

## Current behavior
A queued Intake issue carries `agentflow:triaging` whose description states *"A grounding session is triaging this issue"* even when the record is `waiting` with 0 attempts and no provider family. The operator inspecting the label on GitHub reads active triage where there is none.

## Desired behavior
The `agentflow:triaging` description is true whether the owning record is queued or in a live grounding session — it names an ownership/duplicate-prevention claim and admission, not a running session. It must not assert that a session is currently executing.

## Key interfaces
Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.
- `agentflow/loop.py` — `_claim_triage` (the `gh label create ... --description` string is the whole change) and its symmetric releaser `_release_triage`.
- Traps: the label is (re)created with `--force` on every claim, so the new description propagates fleet-wide the next time any issue is claimed; existing labels keep the old text until then — acceptable, no migration. Keep `_claim_triage`'s create-then-apply logic and its `bool` return contract unchanged; only the description text changes. Do not alter *when* the claim is applied or the ownership/dedup semantics.
- The parallel `agentflow:building` claim (`loop._claim`, description "An agent is building this issue") has the same overclaim shape but is out of scope here.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] The `agentflow:triaging` label description no longer asserts an executing/active session (no "A grounding session is triaging this issue" or equivalent "is triaging now" phrasing); it reads as an ownership + admission claim that is true whether the record is queued or running.
- [ ] `_claim_triage` still creates the label and applies it, and still returns `True`/`False` based on the `gh` return codes — behavior unchanged apart from the description string.
- [ ] Test (regression on the overclaim): monkeypatch `loop._run` to capture the `gh label create` argv for `agentflow:triaging` and assert the `--description` value does not claim a live session and does convey ownership/queue — this test would fail against the current "A grounding session is triaging this issue" text.
- [ ] Test (guards the Live-view premise stays correct): a `waiting` Intake record is omitted from `tracer.live_projection` and therefore accrues no `started_at`/elapsed — documents that queued Intake never renders as a running session.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` green.

## Out of scope
- The console Live board and any new "queued / waiting for admission" panel. Waiting Intake is already correctly omitted from the running projection (no false elapsed time); a distinct queued-work surface is a separate, `/ui-mockups`-gated request, not part of this fix.
- The `agentflow:building` claim description.
- Any change to when the claim is applied or to Intake ownership/duplicate-prevention semantics — the claim must still be set pre-session.

<!-- agentflow:original-below -->
<details>
<summary>Original issue as filed</summary>

## What happened

Two Intake records waited about 50 minutes for Claude capacity with zero attempts and no provider session while another Build held the pool permits. They still appeared as actively triaging, including running-style elapsed time in the Live view. The agentflow:triaging claim description also says a grounding session is triaging the issue even when no session exists.

## What I expected

Waiting Intake work should remain claimed for ownership and duplicate prevention, but it should be presented as queued or waiting for admission. Only records with a live provider session should appear under Live sessions or accrue running time.

## Steps to reproduce

1. Start a Claude Build whose admission demand consumes the pool permit budget.
2. Add two new issues eligible for Intake.
3. Let the daemon claim them while the pool cannot admit another provider attempt.
4. Confirm both records remain waiting with zero attempts, no provider process, and their triaging claims retained.
5. Open the operator console and inspect the Live view and the GitHub claim label.

## Additional context

The triaging label is an ownership claim, not proof of execution. Waiting work consumes neither a permit nor an attempt. The Live contract is executing now, so queued work needs a distinct truthful presentation. If the correction changes the dashboard UI, it must follow the locked mockup gate.

</details>
