Blocked by #154

## Principle (resolved decision — [ADR 0034, shelf-first amendment](https://github.com/ConnorGriffin/agentflow/blob/main/docs/adr/0034-methodology-session-orchestration.md), merged in #166)

Interactive methodology work — grilling above all — runs in the operator's own chat tool (Claude Code or Codex) as ordinary skill sessions. The project workspace is the **artifact surface**: staged Proposals awaiting decision, hash-bound approval, provenanced Publication, pipeline mirror, evidence. This issue builds the bridge between the two: a chat-tool session's resolved output must be able to enter the workspace as a **staged Proposal**, exactly as if an Ask turn had staged it.

## Desired behavior

- From an interactive session in the operator's chat tool (e.g. a `/grilling` or `/wayfinder` session that has worked a decision to a draft build issue), the session can **stage** that draft as a Proposal in the owning project's workspace store.
- The staged Proposal appears on the workspace shelf as a copper "awaiting your decision" card, indistinguishable in lifecycle from one staged by a workspace Ask turn: immutable versions, content-hash identity, staged → approved → published / staged → discarded.
- Approval and Publication go through the existing tracer-#2 machinery (#154): two-beat hash-bound approve in the workspace, idempotent provenanced Publication = build handoff. **The chat-tool session can only stage** — it cannot approve, publish, or write durable truth directly (the ADR 0034 promotion boundary is unchanged).
- Provenance on the Proposal records its origin (chat-tool session, not a workspace Conversation), so a published issue still traces back to what produced it.

## Constraints carried in

- Staging only; daemon-side adoption remains the single door into the workspace store (ADR 0033/0034). The bridge must not open a second write path from outside the daemon.
- The workspace makes no chat investment here: no transcript import, no rendering of the chat-tool conversation. The Proposal (and whatever summary its skill writes into it) is the artifact.
- How the session reaches the store (CLI verb, daemon command endpoint, skill helper) is an implementation choice — but it must be usable from a plain local Claude Code/Codex session on the operator's machine.

## Acceptance

- [ ] An operator-driven local chat session can stage a draft build issue as a Proposal in a named project's workspace; it appears on that project's shelf awaiting decision.
- [ ] The staged Proposal is approvable and publishable through the same flow as an Ask-staged one, with provenance identifying the chat-tool origin.
- [ ] The staging path cannot approve or publish; attempting to is refused.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` passes.

## Out of scope

- Mirroring or rendering chat transcripts in the workspace.
- Any change to workspace Conversation turns, admission, or pacing.
- Publication mechanics themselves (owned by #154).

entries.title: coordinated_research: breadcrumb idempotency guard suppresses on any #N in 'Decisions so far', not just its own entry
entries.body:
*agentflow follow-up — filed from the #189 review.*

## Summary
The idempotency guard that stops a crash-replay from appending a second "Decisions so far" breadcrumb keys on *any* `#N` reference appearing anywhere in that section. If an unrelated existing decision line happens to mention this ticket's number (e.g. "supersedes #240"), the guard reads the breadcrumb as already present and silently skips the append — the research resolution retires without leaving its trail on the map.

This was flagged as a nit during the #189 review (`decision_present`); it is beyond that issue's stated acceptance, hence this follow-up.

## Current behavior
`decision_present` returns true when the ticket's `#N` appears in the "Decisions so far" section at all, regardless of which line carries it. A pre-existing unrelated reference to the same number falsely suppresses the breadcrumb.

## Desired behavior
The guard recognizes only the breadcrumb this resolution actually writes — a decision *entry* for this ticket — not an incidental cross-reference to `#N` inside some other line. A resolution whose number is merely mentioned elsewhere still appends its own line exactly once.

## Key interfaces
Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.
- `agentflow/coordinated_research.py` — `decision_present` (the guard), `with_decision` / `decision_line` (what the append actually writes). Tighten the match to the shape of a written breadcrumb entry rather than a bare `#N` anywhere in the section.
- Keep the guard's fail-closed idempotency: a genuine replay must still find its own already-written line and skip.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] An unrelated `#N` reference elsewhere in "Decisions so far" no longer suppresses this ticket's breadcrumb — the line is appended once.
- [ ] A true replay (this ticket's own breadcrumb already written) is still recognized and not duplicated.
- [ ] Regression test covering both: incidental cross-reference does not suppress; own-line replay does suppress.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` green.

## Out of scope
- The worktree-cleanup follow-up filed alongside this one.
- Any change to what a breadcrumb line looks like or to when resolution runs.

entries.title: coordinated_research: resolved research run's isolated worktree is never cleaned up (resource leak)
entries.body:
*agentflow follow-up — filed from the #189 review.*

## Summary
Each unattended research run provisions an isolated worktree (a detached checkout the session writes its findings artifact into, reused across attempts for resume context). When a run resolves — the ticket is answered, closed, and the map breadcrumb written — that worktree is never removed. Over time resolved runs leave orphaned worktree directories behind: a slow resource leak.

This was flagged as a nit during the #189 review; it is out of scope for that issue, hence this follow-up.

## Current behavior
A resolved research run's isolated worktree persists on disk indefinitely. Nothing prunes it once resolution completes.

## Desired behavior
Once a research run resolves durably (findings posted, ticket closed, breadcrumb present), its isolated worktree is cleaned up. Cleanup must not fire while a run may still resume — an out-of-budget run that drops its claim and becomes available again keeps its worktree so the next attempt resumes the partial findings.

## Key interfaces
Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.
- `agentflow/coordinated_research.py` — `research_worktree` (the path), `_research_worktree_ready` (provisioning via `git worktree add --detach`), and `resolve` (the terminal path where durable resolution is known). Remove the worktree only on the durable-resolution branch.
- Traps: reuse-on-resume is deliberate — a partially-complete run keeps its worktree as-is. Only the terminal resolve path should prune. Use the same `git worktree` machinery the rest of the codebase uses to remove/deregister, not a bare directory delete, so git's worktree registry stays consistent.

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] A durably resolved research run's isolated worktree is removed and deregistered from git.
- [ ] A run that drops its claim without resolving (e.g. out of budget) keeps its worktree so a later attempt resumes.
- [ ] Cleanup tolerates an already-missing worktree without failing resolution.
- [ ] Regression test: resolve removes the worktree; non-resolving exit leaves it in place.
- [ ] `uv run pytest -q` green.

## Out of scope
- The breadcrumb idempotency follow-up filed alongside this one.
- The daemon-restart abandoned-claim cleanup, which already exists.

entries.title: Respond park comment evades every park detector — parked PRs show a stale, wrong reason
entries.body:
## What's wrong

When the Respond stage parks a PR for a human, it posts a comment whose quote line is:

> *agentflow: Respond parked for human review.*

(built at `agentflow/coordinated_build.py:1110` in `_park_respond`).

Every text-based park detector in the pipeline matches the exact substring `"agentflow: parked for human review"` — which that line does **not** contain, because the word `Respond ` is spliced into the middle of it:

- `agentflow/dashboard_data.py:232` — `park_reason()` skips the Respond park comment entirely and falls through to an **older** marker on the PR, so the console shows a stale reason with a wrong "since" timestamp. Live example: agentflow PR #194 is parked by a Respond comment (16:29Z) but the snapshot classifies it as `failed-merge` from an earlier conflict comment (16:15Z) — and the PR is in fact mergeable now.
- `agentflow/runner.py:433` — orphaned review-worktree cleanup treats a Respond-parked PR as *not* parked, so the worktree lingers.
- `agentflow/loop.py:385` — `_finish_review`'s durable-park check misses it the same way.

## The fix

Make the Respond park comment carry the canonical detector substring. Simplest: change the quote line in `_park_respond` (`agentflow/coordinated_build.py:1110`) to:

> *agentflow: parked for human review (Respond).*

so it contains the exact substring `agentflow: parked for human review`. Keep the existing machine-readable `<!-- agentflow-respond-park-target:... -->` proof marker on its own line exactly as it is — `gate.py:45` (`_RESPOND_PARK_TARGET_RE`) and the idempotency check in `_park_respond` (`coordinated_build.py:1108`, `:1119`) depend on it and must keep matching.

Then teach `park_reason()` in `agentflow/dashboard_data.py` to classify a Respond park distinctly is NOT required — with the substring fixed it will classify as `drop-to-reviewed`, which is acceptable. What matters is that the *most recent* park state wins again, per the existing comment-ordering contract at `dashboard_data.py:228`.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A comment body produced by `_park_respond` satisfies all three existing detectors (the substring check in `dashboard_data.park_reason`, `runner.py:433`, `loop.py:385`) — add a test that builds the body the way `_park_respond` does and asserts `park_reason([...])` returns a park (not `None`, and not a stale earlier reason when an older conflict comment precedes it).
2. The `agentflow-respond-park-target` proof marker still round-trips: `_RESPOND_PARK_TARGET_RE` (gate.py:45) still extracts the target id from the new body, covered by a test.
3. Idempotency preserved: a PR that already carries the *old-format* Respond park comment for the same target must not get a second park comment. The existing `already` check keys on the proof marker (`coordinated_build.py:1108`), which is format-independent — add a test proving a re-park against an old-format comment is a no-op.
4. Existing tests stay green (`uv run pytest -q`; note sandbox: use `.venv/bin/pytest` and `AGENTFLOW_STATE=<tmp>` isolation if `~/.agentflow` writes fail).

## Non-goals

- Do not add a new `park_reason` category or touch the console UI — no user-facing surface changes, no screenshots needed.
- Do not change any other park comment format (gate.py:280 etc.).
- Do not touch the Respond verify logic (`_reply_ready`) — that is a separate issue.

entries.title: An exhaustion park with no verdict claims '(no blocking findings)' — reads as a clean review that never happened
entries.body:
## What's wrong

When a review exhausts its budget without producing any verdict, the park handoff posts:

> This PR exhausted its review budget without a durable verdict. Review findings:
> - (no blocking findings)

The second line is fabricated reassurance: there are no findings because there was **no review**, but the rendering is identical to a completed clean review's park. A maintainer reading it (live case: agentflow PR #196) reasonably concludes the PR was reviewed and found clean, and merges unreviewed code.

Mechanism: `park()` (`agentflow/gate.py:274-282`) renders an empty `verdict.findings` as `- (no blocking findings)` unconditionally, and the exhaustion caller (`agentflow/coordinated_build.py:905-908`) passes a findings-less `Verdict(clean=False)` because no verdict exists.

## The fix

Distinguish "reviewed, nothing blocking" from "never reviewed" in the posted body. Smallest honest shape: let the exhaustion caller signal the no-verdict case (e.g. `park(..., verdict=None)` or a keyword flag), and have `park()` render that case as:

> This PR exhausted its review budget without a durable verdict. **No review was completed — do not treat this as a clean review.**

with no findings list at all. All other callers (real verdicts, with or without findings) keep today's rendering exactly.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Pure test on the built body: the no-verdict park contains no `(no blocking findings)` line and contains an explicit not-reviewed sentence; a real clean-verdict park still renders `- (no blocking findings)`; a findings park still renders its findings lines. (The no-verdict case fails before the fix.)
2. The park comment still carries the canonical `agentflow: parked for human review` marker line unchanged (detectors from #197 must keep matching).
3. Suite green: `uv run pytest -q` (sandbox: `.venv/bin/pytest`).

## Non-goals

- No change to when exhaustion parks happen (that's #208's territory) — only to what the comment says.
- No console/UI changes; no screenshots needed.

entries.title: Diverged-review reconciler retires a RUNNING review without terminating its provider session
entries.body:
## What's wrong

Follow-up from the review of PR #213 (issue #208): the diverged-review reconciler retires a review record whose PR head moved even when that record is currently RUNNING a session. The outcome is safe — the permit ledger self-heals and a late verdict for the stale head fails closed — but the orphaned provider process keeps burning tokens reviewing a head that can no longer complete, until it exits on its own.

## The fix

When the reconciler retires (or parks) a review record in RUNNING state, terminate its provider family first, the same way daemon liveness reconciliation kills a dead-record family (reuse that mechanism — the local `os.kill` sweep — not a new one). Only then retire/park. A record whose process is already gone behaves exactly as today.

## Acceptance criteria

1. Reconciler test: a RUNNING diverged review with a live (faked) family → the kill hook is invoked before the record retires; retire still happens if the kill fails (fail-open on termination, fail-closed on verdict already covers safety).
2. WAITING/COMPLETED diverged reviews: no kill attempted (today's behavior pinned).
3. Suite green: `uv run pytest -q` (sandbox: `.venv/bin/pytest`).

## Non-goals

- No change to the retire/park/successor decisions themselves (#208, merged in PR #213).
- No user-facing surface — no screenshots needed.

entries.title: Codebase-memory: exclude daemon worktrees and generated state from the repository index
entries.body:
## Summary

The agentflow codebase-memory index is dominated by daemon residue rather than repository truth. The current index contains 4,187 file nodes; 4,020 (96%) are under `.agentflow/worktrees/`. The local `.agentflow/` tree is 833 MB with roughly 43,000 files, and this repository has no `.cbmignore`.

This makes graph/search results return duplicate historical worktree symbols before current source, wasting retrieval tokens and risking incorrect grounding.

## Desired behavior

Add repository-owned codebase-memory ignore rules that exclude:

- `.agentflow/`
- dependency trees and generated frontend output
- other local/generated artifacts already excluded from normal source review

Rebuild the index and verify current tracked source wins representative searches.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A committed `.cbmignore` excludes daemon worktrees, dependencies, and generated output without excluding current source, tests, ADRs, or research.
- [ ] After reindex, no indexed file path is under `.agentflow/worktrees/`.
- [ ] Representative daemon/coordinator searches resolve current source, not historical worktree copies.
- [ ] Record before/after file/node counts and index size in the PR.
- [ ] Existing test suite remains green.

## Out of scope

Replacing codebase-memory/codegraph; adopting OKF; deleting retained daemon worktrees.

entries.title: Coordinator telemetry: persist per-attempt token spend, cost, duration, and outcome
entries.body:
## Summary

Provider event streams already contain usage data, but agentflow does not normalize or project it. Local preserved Claude artifacts contain input/cache/output tokens, turn counts, duration, model usage, and provider-reported cost; Codex emits turn usage too. Today model-routing policy cannot compare spend with successful outcomes, holds, retries, or revise rounds.

The current local baseline is material: 213 completed Claude runs report a .49 cost equivalent, 412.6M cached-input tokens, and 3.22M output tokens. These facts remain buried in raw event files.

## Desired behavior

Normalize usage at the provider seam and persist it per provider attempt:

- stage, pool, model, provider reasoning effort, and work effort
- input, cached-input/cache-creation, and output tokens
- provider-reported cost when available
- duration, turn count, attempt/restart identity
- terminal cause and verified stage outcome

Expose bounded aggregates suitable for measuring cost per successful stage and per merged issue. Unknown provider fields remain preserved and missing usage remains explicit, never zero-by-assumption.

## Key interfaces

Explore fresh. The provider observation/event parsing, durable coordinator attempt record, and daemon-owned snapshot are the likely seams. Keep raw provider formats behind the provider adapters.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Fixture tests normalize representative Claude and Codex usage events.
- [ ] Each completed attempt persists usage exactly once across daemon restart/reconciliation.
- [ ] Retries and restart replays remain separately attributable.
- [ ] The bounded projection reports totals and missing-data counts by stage/model/outcome.
- [ ] No prompt or provider message content is stored in the aggregate.
- [ ] Existing test suite remains green.

## Out of scope

Changing routing policy, model selection, or the visual console.

entries.title: Intake and review: enforce provider-native structured result schemas
entries.body:
## Summary

Intake and Review require machine-readable terminal decisions, but currently enforce their JSON contracts only through prompt prose. A malformed or missing decision becomes an unverified stage outcome and can trigger another full provider session.

Both installed CLIs expose native schema enforcement: Claude `--json-schema` and Codex `--output-schema`.

## Desired behavior

Define provider-neutral result schemas for Intake and Review, translate them into each runner's native CLI surface, and parse only validated structured output. Keep human-facing Markdown inside typed string fields.

A missing/invalid Intake complexity must not silently upgrade the eventual build to deep. Invalid structured output is an explicit failed outcome with a targeted recovery reason.

## Key interfaces

Explore fresh. Intake/reviewer result parsers own domain validation; runner adapters own CLI-specific schema wiring. Do not leak provider-specific schema details into coordinator policy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Claude and Codex runner tests prove the appropriate native schema is supplied for Intake and Review.
- [ ] Valid ready/grill/mockup and clean/blocking review fixtures parse through the public stage interface.
- [ ] Missing complexity on a ready Intake is invalid rather than defaulting to deep.
- [ ] Invalid output records a typed missing/invalid-result reason without posting partial content.
- [ ] Existing prompt-only JSON extraction is removed once both providers use the schema.
- [ ] Existing test suite remains green.

## Out of scope

Changing which model runs Intake or Review; changing retry budgets.

entries.title: Daemon sessions attach the operator's personal MCP connectors
entries.body:
*agentflow intake — generated by AI.*

## Summary

Daemon-launched Claude sessions attach the operator's three personal claude.ai connectors (Gmail, Google Drive, Google Calendar) even though the launcher passes `--setting-sources project`. That flag governs `settings.json` precedence — it does **not** suppress claude.ai account-synced MCP connectors, which are a separate source. The Claude CLI has a dedicated flag for exactly this: `--strict-mcp-config` ("Only use MCP servers from `--mcp-config`, ignoring all other MCP configurations"). No daemon stage passes `--mcp-config`, so adding `--strict-mcp-config` pins the MCP set to empty for every stage. This is the enforced-by-launch-config fix the ticket asks for.

## Verified

- **Premise confirmed live, not just from the report.** This intake session's own tool surface carries `mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*`, `mcp__claude_ai_Google_Calendar__*`, and `mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__*` — the exact three connectors, attached to an unattended daemon session that has no use for them.
- **The claimed numbers are recorded.** `docs/research/session-profiles-and-ceilings-draft.md` §2b: "82 of 216 Claude sessions loaded three personal MCP servers… 12 sessions had their tool schemas fully expanded into the surface (that is where the 59-tool maximum comes from)." It also states plainly: "`--setting-sources project` was meant to exclude user config, yet the MCP servers still attach; a narrow profile that pins the MCP set to empty closes this leak outright."
- **The decision is already sanctioned.** ADR 0044 §2 (accepted 2026-07-19): "MCP servers are pinned to empty for every stage. Personal connectors never attach to daemon sessions (tracked independently as #240)." So this ticket owns the MCP-empty pin, decoupled from the broader per-stage profile work — no ADR contradiction.
- **Single launch funnel.** Every daemon Claude session — Intake, Review, Build, Respond, Revise, Converse, Mockup, Research — is built by one function: `ClaudeRunner.structured_argv` in `agentflow/runner.py`, called through `ClaudeProviderAdapter.command` in `agentflow/coordinator/providers.py`. No stage passes `--mcp-config`. One flag added there covers all stages.

## Current behavior

The argv built in `structured_argv` is `claude -p … --model … --output-format stream-json --verbose --permission-mode acceptEdits --setting-sources project --settings <inline>` (+ `--json-schema` when a stage supplies a result contract). No MCP-scoping flag is present, so claude.ai account connectors attach: 82/216 sessions (2026-07-16→07-19) loaded all three, and 12 expanded full schemas into the surface, pushing one session to 59 loaded tools — paid cache-creation waste on every affected launch, plus personal accounts reachable from unattended sessions.

## Desired behavior

A daemon Claude session loads **zero** MCP servers. No `mcp__claude_ai_*` (or any other) MCP tool appears in the tool surface, enforced by the launch argv itself, not by settings convention.

## Key interfaces

Explore fresh; pointers, not line numbers.

- `ClaudeRunner.structured_argv` in `agentflow/runner.py` — the one place the Claude command is assembled. Add `--strict-mcp-config` here. Because no `--mcp-config` is passed anywhere, this alone yields an empty MCP set.
- `agentflow/coordinator/providers.py` `ClaudeProviderAdapter.command` — confirms `structured_argv` is the sole call site for all stages; nothing else to touch.
- Test anchor: `tests/test_runner.py` already asserts on the Claude argv (`--setting-sources`, `--settings`, `--json-schema`). Add the regression assertion alongside those.
- **Trap:** do not touch the `CodexRunner` path — it already isolates config via `--ignore-user-config`/`--ephemeral`; this ticket is Claude-only. Also do not add `--mcp-config` pointing at a file; the goal is an *empty* set, and `--strict-mcp-config` alone achieves it.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `ClaudeRunner.structured_argv` includes `--strict-mcp-config` in the emitted argv for every stage/model/schema combination.
- [ ] A daemon-launched (or replayed) Claude session's recorded tool list contains no `mcp__claude_ai_Gmail__*`, `mcp__claude_ai_Google_Calendar__*`, or `mcp__claude_ai_Google_Drive__*` tools — and no MCP tools of any kind.
- [ ] Regression test in `tests/test_runner.py`: assert `--strict-mcp-config` is present in `ClaudeRunner().structured_argv(...)` output (with and without a `schema`). This test fails if the flag is ever dropped.
- [ ] `--setting-sources project` and `--settings <inline>` remain unchanged; the sandbox/network settings block is untouched.

## Out of scope

- Per-stage tool allowlists, spend ceilings, and wall-clock/turn ceilings — ADR 0044 / wayfinder #231 own those.
- The read-only-stage edit-tool removal (also #231/ADR 0044).
- Any Codex-path change.
- Introducing a curated MCP allowlist for stages that might later want a specific server; if that need arises it is a separate ticket. This one pins to empty.

## Outcome
